Run the CI flake sweep nightly and unattended, so the MIND flake backlog stays reconciled without anyone remembering to trigger it. Because a *full-window* sweep is the only path permitted to close stale flake tickets, a sweep that only happens ad hoc leaves fixed flakes filed forever and new ones unfiled.

New `.github/workflows/flake-sweep-scheduled.yml` runs daily at 13:00 UTC (clear of TMR's 08:00 UTC window and its 4-hour worst case) and is also manually dispatchable. It checks out `main` with full history -- the skill scopes evidence to post-fix commits with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, which a shallow clone cannot answer -- installs Python, uv, the project, the pinned Claude Code CLI and the pinned latchkey CLI, pre-trusts the checkout so Claude Code does not block on its trust dialog, and pulls `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LINEAR_FLAKE_SWEEP_API_KEY` from Vault over GitHub OIDC. Since `scripts/flake_reconcile.py` reaches Linear through `latchkey curl`, the Linear token is installed into latchkey rather than exported, which is why the script itself needed no change at all. The job then preflights both credentials -- a read-only `flake_reconcile.py list-tickets` must reach Linear, and `gh` must be able to read both `actions/runs` and `check-runs` -- so a bad credential fails in seconds instead of ninety minutes into an Opus run. The Linear probe deliberately runs the real call rather than inspecting `latchkey services info`: that command's `credentialStatus` field exists in latchkey 2.x but not in the pinned 3.10.0, so reading it silently reports "unset" against a current CLI. `manage-flakes`' stated precondition had the same staleness and is corrected to the same read-only probe. It deliberately does not reuse `.github/actions/tmr-setup`: that action changes with TMR's orchestrator, and a little duplication is cheaper than a dependency shifting under a job nobody watches. Permissions are read-only on the repo (`contents`, `actions`, `checks`) plus `id-token` for Vault; the job writes nothing back to git.

Both flake skills gained an `--autonomous` mode that changes exactly two things and nothing else: `manage-flakes` stops pausing for approval, and a run summary must be written. Critically it does **not** collapse the skill's structure -- an autonomous run still writes out the same plan it would have shown a human, *then* applies it, *then* appends what actually changed. That narration is load-bearing rather than ceremony: it is the only record of intent if a write goes wrong, and stating a plan before acting measurably improves how faithfully it is followed. Every existing guard still holds unattended -- closes remain restricted to full-window sweeps with a `last-seen` older than 21 days, and a human's or agent's state move on a ticket is still never clobbered. `manage-flakes` accepts the flag directly as well as via `detect-flakes`, so future automation can drive it standalone; `report-incidental-flakes` is untouched and stays interactive and create/update-only. Without the flag both skills behave exactly as before.

Fixes a real, pre-existing bug in `scripts/flake_reconcile.py`: it read each commit's check-runs with `gh api --paginate` and parsed the result with a single `json.loads`. On an object-returning endpoint `--paginate` emits one bare JSON object per page, concatenated, which is not valid JSON -- so any commit with enough check-runs to paginate (100+) aborted the entire sweep and took the whole window's flake data with it. Fixed with `--slurp`, which wraps the pages in an array, plus a pure `merge_check_run_pages` helper and unit tests. A sweep only trips this when some commit in its window is busy enough, which is why it went unnoticed.

The sweep also moved out of the agent and into its own workflow step. It reads ~2000 commits and outruns an agent's per-command timeout, so an agent asked to run it has no option but to background it, and then loses it when its turn ends. A workflow step has no such ceiling, so the deterministic fetch runs there and Claude gets only the clustering and reconciliation. That is the split the CLI was designed around: it moves data and never clusters. `detect-flakes` now uses a pre-populated `/tmp/flakes.json` when one exists and sweeps for itself otherwise, so interactive use is unchanged.

`detect-flakes` also gains an explicit rule that unattended runs must finish inside a single turn. Backgrounding work and reporting back later is correct interactively, where the harness wakes the agent when it finishes, but fatal under `claude -p`, where ending the turn terminates the process and kills the backgrounded work. The workflow also fails any run that produced no `/tmp/flakes.json`, so a sweep that did not run cannot read as success.

The Slack post is also the last step in the job and reports `job.status` rather than any single step's outcome. Keying it off one step would let a failure in a later guard still post a green heartbeat, and a heartbeat that can claim green on a red run is worse than none, since its whole premise is that green means healthy.

Reporting is a heartbeat rather than an alarm: the skill writes `flake-sweep-summary.md`, which the job renders verbatim into both the GitHub job summary and a Slack post to `#minds-notifications` (via a new `mngr/ci/SLACK_FLAKE_SWEEP_WEBHOOK` Vault entry, warning-and-skipping when unset, as the existing minds CI notification does). Every run posts, including one that changed nothing, so silence means breakage; a failed run or a missing summary posts a failure notice and fails the job, since a sweep that wrote no summary cannot be verified and must not read as green. The summary, Claude's log and the sweep's JSON intermediates upload as a 30-day artifact so a bad night stays diagnosable.

The `bump-latchkey` skill now covers five pins rather than four, adding the flake-sweep workflow's `npm install -g latchkey@X.Y.Z`. Because that pin is just a literal in a workflow file, a missed bump would otherwise surface only as a failed nightly sweep, so `apps/minds/imbue/minds/test_latchkey_version_alignment.py` now also asserts it equals the remote-host pin. Pin 4 lives in another repo and remains checked by nobody.

Also adds `blueprint/nightly-flake-sweep-ci/`, the design doc this was built from, which records the Linear and Vault accesses the job depends on.
